Peterium is infested with the worst kind of pirates - the type that don't even have a theme song. Get in, do what you do, pull the meat core. The "chum" in the title is not referring to you. Probably.
Sub Zeroni has a frost problem, a creature problem, and a morale problem. None of those are technically your problem. Your problem is the meat core. Everything else is weather.

Lava Del Rey is MAGNIFICENT, Squishy! The heat! The glow! The complete structural instability of literally everything! Most employees won't even GO there, which is their loss (and also statistically related to the fatalities.) If you ask me, it's a PERFECTLY reasonable place to send an employee.
Big Ol' Tangus is exactly what it sounds like: big, ornery, and full of things that want to stop your engines. Show 'em you've got better engines. Get the meat core. Go home.

A lot of great stories start with climbing a dangerous mountain, Squishy. This could be one of those stories. Or it could just be work. Either way you're climbing it. The meat core is up there somewhere.
Don't let "Li'l" fool you. Li'l Tangus has a real big chip on its shoulder. Last three extraction teams came back confused about what happened. You'll do great. Probably.

Welcome to Rangus Meats, li'l buddy! Now, the only thing standing between you and Employee of the Month is meat, and the only thing standing between you and meat is whatever's out there trying to bite your face off. So go on out there, get a meat core, and pop it right out so we can feed the galaxy! That's the whole gig in a nutshell!

Every Rangus hire spends time in their first week doing some R&D (that's "Research & Demolition" to you, li'l buddy). And there’s a big ‘ol world of violence…I mean “research” waiting to be done. Show me what you can do and we’ll see about upgrading those weapons.

There’s more on those planets than just meat little buddy…bring me back a load of minerals and I'll have the shop manufacture you a very fine excavation tool. Strictly for the careful retrieval of historical relics, of course. (And anything that happens to be holding them.)

Those ancient gastronauts left a lot of useful junk laying around the galaxy! And Rangus has a "finders keepers" policy that legal has reviewed exactly zero times. Haul me back some ancient tech and I'll rig you up a little something to make the next planet even more bountiful.
Now you're looking good, that's worth another TIP or two.

Well Squishy, I see you been gatherin' resources like a big ol' squirrel storin' nuts for the winter. That's good!

Now it's time to become that super squishy we know you oughta be.

You know what you need to get noticed around here? Some oomph…pizazz…Flair! Like those enemies that are glowing gold. That's the look we want for you. Take 'em down, take their shine, and let's get a little sparkle on that uniform.

My good buddy Mike runs the best little exchange counter in the sector: fair rates, fair smiles, fair number of fingers...I think we can convince him to set up shop on the ship full-time, but Mike's a businessman. Show him there's good money to be made off you and he'll come around real quick.
I see that look in your eye, Squishy... you just found out there's a ranking system. Good! Keep climbing! There's a little something in it for ya, and I mean that literally: it's quite small.

I had a picture of you printed up for the breakroom wall. It's not a great picture but it showed your spirit. I don't remember what happened to it, but keep ranking up! There's a bonus in it somewhere, and you've earned it.

A lot of employees quit right around here. Thought rank 30 was good enough. Those folks are sandwiches now...not a punishment, they were just reassigned. You're better than a sandwich, Squishy. Probably.
You know what I love about you? You just keep going. Some employees hit rank 30 and just phone it in. Not you. You're something else. Now get back to work.
In terms of calendar time you've been an employee for considerably less than a decade. But emotionally? Decades. Real deep, meaty decades. The bonus is real though.
The Employee of the Century award used to be given posthumously. We're trying a new approach. You're making history here, Squishy. And more importantly: you're making money.
I have never...not once...handed out an Employee of the Millennium award. You'd be the first. Think about that. I mean it. Think about it while you keep ranking up.
We're getting into territory where I had to look up what the words mean. Geologically speaking, an epoch is a very long time. In employee-recognition terms, it means you're kind of unbelievable.
Squishy. Buddy. I'm running out of time increments. An aeon is a billion years. No company has operated for a billion years. We are pushing the limits of HR here and I respect it.

You did it. I had a trophy made - it's shaped like a meat patty. It says your name on it, except I didn't know your name so it says "Squishy." That IS your name, right? Congratulations. I mean every word.
Squishy, the aquatic menu has been underperforming and I need samples. Grab that fishin' pole, find yourself some Water Rifts, and bring back everything you catch. Don't ask what we're doing with it.
I know "Slime Rift" doesn't sound appetizing. Neither does "processed meat product" and that's our best seller. Trust the process, Squishy. Get in there and fish.

Rangus Corp's entire mineral acquisition department is you. No budget. No equipment. No backup. Get out there and dig up every kind of mineral you can find. That's not a problem — that's an opportunity.

At Rangus Corp, we love innovation. We also love finding out what other folks already innovated and then acquiring it. Legally. Mostly. Gather every kind of ancient tech you can find. Call it "competitor research".

Complete a system on Hot Difficulty to unlock a greater challenge and even more rewards.
Complete a system on Blazing Difficulty to unlock the thrilling Nightmare Difficulty.
The Grenade Launcher is not technically recommended for close-quarters work. But someone who clears 250 Prime Directives with one? That's a person who figured something out.
The Magnum announces itself. It says "I am here and I mean it." Two hundred and fifty Prime Directives. Let it do the talking.
A good employee knows their tools. A great employee masters one. Show me what a Pistol can really do, Squishy. I'll be watching.
The Plasma Caster was my personal choice back in the field days. Elegant. Efficient. Unreasonable at close range. Two hundred and fifty Prime Directives - let's see if you've got the touch.
The Rail Gun requires patience, precision, and a complete disregard for collateral damage.
The Rifle is the reliable one. Never flashy, always there. Some employees overlook the Rifle. Those employees are wrong. Two hundred and fifty Prime Directives - show some respect.
I have a specific type of employee who asks for the Rocket Launcher. Know what they all have in common? Results.
The Shotgun is a philosophy, Squishy. Wide. Committed. Leaves no question unanswered. 250 Prime Directives, Squishy. I expect enthusiasm.
An SMG says "I have a lot to say and I'm going to say all of it very quickly." I respect that energy. Let's see how quick you can clear those Prime Directives.

Rangus prefers a well-rounded employee, li'l buddy — and "well-rounded" in this department means fluent in artillery. Get yourself one of every weapon and put some live-fire hours on each. I want your name on the wall down at the range before the next quarterly review.

Squishy, I'm looking at your swap numbers and I don't know if this is art or a medical condition - but you have a GIFT. Keep going. Let's see how high that number gets. For science. And also for reasons I can't disclose to HR.
Medium's the sensible order, Squishy — enough heat to keep you honest, not so much the galaxy eats you alive. That's a legitimate way to play. Rangus Corp supports work-life balance. Mostly.

Hot. A notch past the house recommendation — for when the easy runs stop keeping you up at night. Not too gentle, not too harrowing, and exactly as dangerous as the liability waiver covers. Go have yourself a run.
Blazing. I ran Blazing back in my field days and I did not enjoy it. But I respect it enormously. You come back from this and we're having a serious talk about your future here.
I'm not going to lie to you — I don't send employees into Nightmare mode. You would have to go there yourself, of your own free will. I just want it on record that I had mixed feelings on this one.
Squishy. Twenty-five planets. I need you to evacuate from twenty-five planets. I told the whole crew this plan was already underway. I said it was going great. So we need to get it going.

Fifty planets. Here's the thing — I may have told someone you were already at fifty. I don't remember why I said that. But I said it, and they know I said it, and I need the number to actually be fifty now.
Seventy-five planets evacuated. The travel department flagged your records - turns out there IS a leaderboard and you are on it. Top ten, last I checked.

I went to a dinner. I said some things at the dinner. About you. About your evacuation numbers specifically. Big numbers. Everyone at the dinner seemed very impressed and I need those numbers to be real now. A hundred planets, Squishy. Please.

I gave a speech. At an industry conference. I said your name. I said a number. I said that number was already achieved and that you were the greatest evacuator in Rangus Corp history. There was applause. I cannot undo the applause. A hundred and fifty planets.
That Fish Came From the Moon

Our lunar offerings are a mystery — even to me, and I'm the one selling them. Do some recon for me would 'ya? Find the Lunar Rifts, catch what's in there, and report back. This is research. We're calling it research.
Look, Squishy — fishing in a Sludge Rift is not glamorous work. But you're made of meat, and that's not glamorous either...but here you are. Catch everything. Wear gloves. Probably.
Brine Rift fish is our most premium menu item. Customers pay triple for it and don't know why. Neither do I. That's fine. Catch everything in there and don't fall in.
Presentation matters, Squishy. I built this company on great meat AND great presentation. Ten flair is a solid start. You're starting to look like somebody out there.
There's a saying in the restaurant business: twenty-five pieces of flair is the minimum. I made that saying up, but it's right. Keep collecting - you're representing Rangus Corp out there!
Fifty flair. I looked up "debonair" to make sure I was using it right. I was. This is exactly what that word was invented for. Keep going.

Now, I'm not going to tell you to collect a hundred flair. That's not something I would ever tell you to do. I just want you to think about what a hundred flair would say about you as a person. As an employee. Anyway. It's completely up to you.

Here at Rangus we’ve had to create some "unique" departments for a fast food chain. Turns out feeding the galaxy isn't just sandwiches and smiles, it's harder than it looks! Head down to Weapon R&D and start ranking up your kit. The more variety on your hip, the easier meat will be to procure.
Squishy, bring me some of those rocks and ancient tech. We'll get you equipped with the latest in dimensional rift fishing gear so you can catch some big ones.
Use that dimensional rift fishing gear and catch a few big ones!

Around here, "self-improvement" isn't a suggestion - it's a performance metric. It's also an official workplace benefit! Head over to the Employee Benefits Terminal and unlock a fresh upgrade for yourself. Show me you're growing into the role, li'l buddy.

I have a very sharp prize locked up in the equipment locker and I have been looking for an excuse to give it out. You look like you can earn it. Go hit some stuff and come back. I'll know if you did good.
You passed your probation, congratulations! Now we can get into the real work and see if you have what it takes.
You’re new here so we gotta see what your skills are like and help you hone all the areas we need for you to be the best employee you can be!
You really go above and beyond the call of duty! We like your spunk and as a reward would like to give you even more responsibilities! Isn’t work fun?
Now that you know the ropes around here we can start getting you prepped for more duties and responsibilities! Always need more employees looking to take on more.

Mike's on the ship! But settling in is a whole thing for him, and the man runs on goodwill and fish guts in roughly that order. Do us a favor and sell him a load of fish, the smellier the better. He'll be family by the end of the week, mark my words.

We need a lot of meat to feed the galaxy and management likes a go-getter! Get out there and bring in a real haul of meat cores; the kind of number that makes the accountants do a little dance. Stack 'em high, Squishy. There's a corner office in your future.
What do you think of a person who only does the bare minimum? Yeah, me neither. Equip that flair you earned and walk into work looking like Employee of the Month. Appearances matter in fast food.

We've been getting reports of weird little structures out there...locals are calling 'em "shrines." Best we can tell, tapping into one juices up whoever's standing nearest. Go figure out how they work for us, would you? If the galaxy's handing out free power-ups, Rangus wants the receipt.

When you run into those big boss baddies out in the field, don't just kill 'em; sample 'em. There's something real special cookin' in that meat, and the lab boys downstairs have been begging me for fresh material. Bring me back the good stuff and I'll make sure they remember whose name was on the cooler.

Those aliens are up to something...I can feel it in my gut, and my gut runs this company. They've been summoning big ol' Zordbeams and tucking 'em behind shields like they're hiding something. Take out their summoning rigs before whatever they're cookin' gets too cooked.

Heads up — we've been seeing turrets sproutin' on planets like dandelions, and a Harvester catching crossfire is a Harvester I can't insure. Go knock 'em down before they all decide to fire on the same target at the same time. Keep the supply line clean, Squishy.

You ever crack open one of those Mystery Meat Cubes the enemies drop? Real strange stuff inside...and "strange" is just "valuable" with extra steps. Go bust some open for us, would you? Whatever's in there, Rangus owns it now.

My buddy Coach Dan's been on the horn; some mutants are running drills on him out on Ol' Tangus and he's gettin' a little crabby about it. Head down there, run with him for a bit, and remind those mutants whose galaxy this is. Do an old friend a solid.

We’ve been trying to track down a mysterious radio transmission but it’s all garbled. There's a network of old radio towers scattered across the planets. Fire 'em up one by one and let's see if we can clean that signal up. Could be nothing. Could be very much not nothing.

The pinnacle of Meat Science achievement. A colossal construct of dense, reinforced meat capable of devastating combat performance. Carl Rangus designed it for situations that called for less finesse and more everything else.

A territorial aerial combatant found throughout the galaxy's less pleasant environments. The venom is bad. The sound is somehow worse. Rangus Meats has, on at least three occasions, attempted to incorporate it into a menu item. All three occasions ended the same way.
Former customer of Rangus Meats. Current threat to its employees. Extended Glizzy Gulp consumption has done remarkable things for his physique and absolutely nothing for his temperament.

Manufactured by the Rangus Meats Automated Defense Division before the Automated Defense Division was quietly discontinued. Still operational. Still following the last orders it received. Nobody remembers what those orders were.
Eight legs. Several eyes. One opinion about your presence here, and it is not a welcoming one. Found in webs of its own design that it is very proud of.

The crowning achievement of Project Leviathan and the crowning failure of Rangus Meats aquacultural experimentation. Whatever it was before the algae, it is something considerably larger now.

It is unclear whether it is angry. It is very clear that it is hungry.
A reconnaissance and combat vessel operated by alien forces whose motivations remain poorly documented. It moves fast, shoots accurately, and has never once complied with a hailing frequency.
Dramatically enlarged by generations of Meat Science runoff contaminating the freshwater systems of Peterium. Technically still a frog. Not technically safe to be near.
The native piranha population of Peterium was considered a minor nuisance before Project Leviathan began. That was a long time ago.
Enhanced through sustained exposure to experimental Meat Science compounds. Faster. Larger. More interested in you than any shark has any right to be.
A free-floating ocular organism with no visible body and no apparent explanation. Rangus Meats xenobiologists have filed numerous reports about it. None of the reports agree on what it is.
A basic SmartMeat construct that has gone feral or been repurposed by hostile forces. Simple. Determined. Surprisingly durable for something that is, at its core, just meat.
Once employed in a Rangus Meats processing facility. Retained the tools of the trade through several career transitions that were not entirely voluntary.
Grease Monkey is a decommissioned auto-mechanic bot that never got the memo it's been replaced. Kill it for wrenches that heal friendly structures better than they ever fixed a car.

Formerly a scientist working for Rangus Meats, this enormous creature now sees himself as both the guardian of the aquatic life of Peterium and also the world's apex predator.

He also thinks he's a pirate. People sure are strange!
A creature defined by its enormous ocular apparatus and its apparent compulsion to stare at everything it encounters before consuming it. The staring is a warning. Most things learn this too late.
A Franken Meats vessel that delivers additional horrors to wherever additional horrors are needed. It does not land so much as it deposits its contents and departs.

Unfortunately, not all Meat Science experiments resulted in giant leaps forward for civilization. What began as a small-scale project aimed at enhancing porcine subjects with XXXtreme Flavor (TM) quickly spiraled out of control. Instead of creating a perfect food, the technicians from Rangus Meats created a perfect eating machine.

This mindless creature, dubbed Franken Beans by one of the scientists shortly before he was consumed along with his team, now travels through the galaxy in an endless quest to sate its hunger.

The result of a Meat Science experiment conducted in the spirit of inquiry and concluded in the spirit of deeply regretting that spirit.

Half man. Half wasp. All problem.
A stationary weapons platform with no agenda, no feelings, and no intention of letting you pass. Of all the enemies you will face, this one is arguably the most honest about what it wants.
A creature of uncertain origin whose limbs extend far beyond what biomechanics typically permit. It uses this to its advantage. You will find this out shortly.
Smaller, faster, and no less hungry than its creator. The Franken Meats appetite is hereditary. The portion size is the only thing that has decreased.
A SmartMeat construct that has exceeded its recommended growth parameters by a significant margin. Whoever approved its development specifications has not been available for comment.
A compact but formidable cosmic combatant who compensates for a reduced range of motion with an increased commitment to applying that motion to your face.
Does not fight back. Does not move. Has, against all reasonable expectation, survived this long. This says more about the shooting range than the target.
Operates at distances that suggest either very good equipment or very personal reasons. Possibly both. Has not filed a statement either way.
Achieved aerial dominance through the acquisition of technology it was almost certainly not supposed to have. Fast, maneuverable, and extremely confident about both.
Solved the locomotion problem by eliminating it entirely. Hovers at a consistent altitude that happens to be exactly at threat level. This is not a coincidence.
Small. Extremely built. Operating under the assumption that size is merely a number, and that number is not relevant to the fight it is about to start.
A duck-shaped rock formation that has, at some point in its geological history, become aggressively animate. The Rangus Meats Geology Division submitted a paper about this. The paper was rejected.
A subterranean humanoid with excellent tunneling instincts and poor opinions about visitors. Surfaces only when provoked. Is frequently provoked.
A Glizzy Gulp-fueled transport operated by the Mutant faction. Arrives fast. Leaves faster. What it deposits in between is your problem now.
Alien transport vessel optimized for rapid deployment of forces and equally rapid departure from the consequences of that deployment.
It keeps going. More of them keep coming out of it. The mathematics of this have not been explained and will not be explained. Just keep shooting.

This strange but friendly robot's origin is unknown. Some believe he arrived in a craft from a distant galaxy, quite a spell ago.

Most recently, Reset was encountered as a prisoner of the sentient long-range robot factory called Calypso, apparently as a result of a failed relationship between the two entities.
An automated weapons platform that someone had the foresight to remove from the ground. It did not make it friendlier. It made it harder to avoid.
A smaller concentration of Glizzy Gulp dependency than the full-sized model, but no less committed to the core mission of causing problems.
A detached ocular unit functioning independently of any host. Deployed for surveillance, escalated to direct engagement. The transition was not in the original specs.
The first stage of Beatrice's deployment cycle. Small. Unassuming. Already counting down.
Tall in the way that suggests the home planet's gravity had strong opinions about vertical growth. Uses the height advantage constantly and without apology.
Oversees combat with an authority that nobody voted on and nobody has successfully challenged. Calls it as it sees it. Sees everything.
A bureaucratic combatant deployed by Pork Barrel Pete to entangle opponents in procedural delays and physical damage simultaneously. The paperwork is a weapon. The weapon is also a weapon.
Fresh from the campaign trail and absolutely certain that this is what public service looks like. Arrives in large numbers. Votes along party lines.
Presides over the arena with the absolute certainty of someone who has never once questioned their own judgment. The gavel is enormous. The rulings are final.
A corporate enforcement unit operating on behalf of the Pounding Fathers administration. Carries out decisions. Does not make them. Does not need to.
Beatrice at full deployment. Whatever you were doing, stop doing it.
Low center of gravity. High threshold for pain. The Glizzy Gulp mutations didn't make him taller, but they made the height he has considerably more effective.
A Duckstone unit that has been, through means that remain classified, inducted into some form of official capacity. The badge is real. The duck is real. The rock is also real.
Beatrice, midway through her growth cycle. Larger than she looks. Already making plans.
A heavily armored ground vehicle operated by the Machine faction. Named Tommy by someone in the manufacturing chain who wanted to be remembered. Tommy is not a comforting presence.
A directed-energy weapons platform with excellent range and strong opinions about everything within that range.

Doctor Brad Sideman is the lead researcher on Project Leviathan, which focuses on maximizing the efficiency of aquatic protein sources for Rangus Meats. Sideman's team showed great promise, developing strains of algae that spurred hypertrophy in organisms consuming it. Unexpected mutations were noted as "controllable outliers."

Sadly, the project was shuttered due to budget reallocations. All supply drops to the planet were canceled. No record of team extraction exists on file, but Dr. Sideman continued to post in his log until this final entry:

The hunger brings clarity. I understand now. I am the captain ... I am the white whale ... I am the harpoon. I am guardian and predator. I am the ocean itself, eternal and alone.

This mindless creature, dubbed Franken Beans by one of the scientists shortly before he was consumed along with his team, now travels through the galaxy in an endless quest to sate its hunger.

This grizzled trainer is widely renowned for producing championship fighters across dozens of worlds.

After his corporate sponsorship from Rangus Meats lapsed, Coach Dan retreated from public life to the pastoral region of Mount Dangus.

As Rangus Meats took over the food-production segment of galactic commerce, top executive Dorothy Duncan realized that they needed a companion beverage to serve alongside their brightly-wrapped sandwiches and fried snacks. Thus was born Glizzy Gulp.

Equal parts hyper-sweetened beverage and ultra-energy drink, this delicious creation falls just under the government-regulated threshold for a controlled substance.

Its recipe is a highly guarded secret, and unauthorized attempts to recreate it frequently result in spontaneous combustion.

Glizzy Gulp. For every part of your day.

The home planet of Carl Rangus became the first galactic headquarters of Rangus Meats.

The corporate offices were relocated following an industrial accident some years ago.

This rift, located on Esfera De Carne, was once a small and highly controlled method of extracting the protein-rich Omni Meat from its native dimension.

The recklessness of Rangus Meats and its founder, Carl Rangus, led to its over-expansion and the catastrophe known as the Omni Meat Incident.

As the galaxy's population grew, the demand for Omni Meat skyrocketed. At first, Carl Rangus tightly controlled the use of the Omni Meat Portal, but stronger voices among corporate leadership at Rangus Meats convinced him to widen the portal.

This did not proceed as planned.

Omni Meat exploded from the portal at an uncontrollable rate. It spread unchecked across Rangus Prime and throughout Omnikron, infecting and transmuting worlds and their populations. Before long the entire galaxy had become tainted by Omni Meat.

Dorothy "Dottie" Duncan began her career as the silent partner to Carl Rangus in the founding of Rangus Meats.

As the company grew, she took on a larger and larger role focused on finance and marketing, allowing Carl to continue developing new breakthroughs in Meat Science.

Dottie was lost during the tragic Omni Portal Incident. Carl still holds out a sliver of hope that he'll find her one day.
This heavily populated system is home to over 23 billion customers, most of them living on the primary world, Big Ol' Tangus.

This sparsely populated planetary system was once heavily used by Rangus Meats for testing and research.

Thanks to increased efficiency, most facilities here are no longer in active operation.

The founder of Rangus Meats, a restaurant chain that grew into a galactic superpower, began as a humble inventor looking to reinvent the business model of making and serving food.

His innovative Meat Science breakthroughs disrupted the paradigm and ushered in a bright new age of happy customers and full bellies. He is beloved by the galaxy.

After his departure from the company, the site was quietly closed and eliminated from the budget. No funding was allocated for staff reassignment.

The primary world of Plumtor's Folly is heavily populated by a largely urban population of humanoids. Generations of exposure to the substance known as Glizzy Gulp (a registered trademark of Rangus Meats) have permanently altered the population's DNA in strange, unexplainable ways.

Big Ol' Tangus selects its rulers through a system of ritualized combat that also serves as the primary form of entertainment. This ensures that only the strongest celebrities rise to positions of authority over the people.

Once an idyllic escape from the crumbling urban centers of Big Ol' Tangus, this region was largely abandoned after becoming overrun by Mutants and Franken creatures.

The area's most notable inhabitant is a retired fight trainer named Coach Dan.

As the galaxy's thirst for Glizzy Gulp grew wildly, one forward-thinking executive at Rangus Meats engineered the purchase of this moon for a new factory site.

Over time, Li'l Tangus grew into the galactic manufacturing hub for Glizzy Gulp, supplying billions of gallons a day to an audience that craves more and more each year.

This triumvirate of championship-level fighters rules Plumtor's Folly thanks to their string of victories at Monday Night Midterms, the ritual combat used to select leaders.

Pork Barrel Pete wields bureaucracy to defend himself while summoning Junior Senators to overwhelm his opponents.

Hair Force One flies overhead, devastating his opponent with bombs and clever quips.

Judge Crawdaddy rules the ring with his barrage of justice-aimed hammers.

Today, Carl Rangus uses the planet as a testing ground for his latest generation of Meat Scientists.

This branch of industrialized bioengineering was pioneered by inventor-disruptor Carl Rangus.

He used it to feed a hungry galaxy through his company, Rangus Meats.

Countless competitors have tried and failed to replicate his closely held trade secrets.

When Carl Rangus' Meat Science wasn't enough to feed the hungry galaxy, he explored more unorthodox approaches.  


One experiment pierced the barrier between dimensions and revealed an entire universe filled with an organic, protein-based substance Carl dubbed Omni Meat.  This endless supply of edible material (and starship fuel) enabled Rangus Meats to massively expand its operations. 


Hunger was eliminated. The galaxy thrived and grew.

BartY Que was the folksy, gunslinging mascot of Rangus Meats ‘Rangusland’ and featured on the Rangus Power Hour. Dressed like a multiarmed cowboy with a big grin and two pairs of smoking meat shooters (no peas allowed!) Barty traveled the galactic frontier spreading the good word of premium Rangus products.

Part salesman, and part hero,he always seemed to have a clever quip and a barbecue-themed solution for every problem. His friendly and down home charm made him one of the leaders of the Rangusland crew.

Barkesly the JPG Dog was one of the most beloved stars of the classic Rangus Power Hour, a wildly popular children's adventure show that mixed comedy, lessons, and questionable meat science.

Barkesly originally discovered as an ancient corrupted image file floating through the Borf Nebula, Barkesly’s antics delighted audiences across the galaxy. Barking her famous catchphrase, "Hold on, I'm buffering!", became one of the most quoted lines in meat-y-vision history, and her loyal friendship with the crew of Rangusland helped make the Rangus Power Hour a cultural phenomenon for an entire generation.

Mr. E. Meat was the Rangus Power Hour’s resident goof, an armless, lanky two-legged, chaotic oddball of meat cuts who rarely spoke actual words, but instead communicated through a baffling collection of whistles, honks, and exaggerated gestures. Though he appeared clueless and constantly stumbled into trouble, Mr. E. Meat somehow always possessed the answer to the crew’s biggest problems.

Known for breaking the fourth wall and frequently reacting to the viewing audience, he became one of the show's most memorable characters. His unpredictable antics made him a fan favorite and a source of endless adoration among viewers.

Professor Chickelous Nuggetmon was the Rangus Power Hour’s resident know it all, a scholarly owl-like genius who claimed to hold seventeen doctorates and at least three coupon cards for free chicken nuggets. Always presenting a seemingly endless supply of charts, and graphs, he spent his days conducting bizarre experiments and explaining the known universe through the principles of breading, dipping, and proper nugget formation.

While his inventions had a tendency to explode, hatch, or become unexpectedly sentient (see MR E MEAT), they somehow worked often enough to keep him part of the crew. Known for peppering every lecture with terrible chicken jokes and wildly overcomplicated explanations, Professor Nuggetmon was a beloved source of both scientific wisdom and fowl-based laughter.

Nacho Grande was the Rangus Power Hour’s flamboyant master of flair, a dramatic fast-food beef-fighter who treated every obstacle, no matter how large or how small, like a grand performance. Dressed in an elaborate matador outfit covered in flashy flair, he charged fearlessly into danger with style, flash, and absolutely no subtlety.

Whether twirling his cape, striking heroic poses, or delivering over the top speeches, Nacho believed that if something was worth doing, it was worth doing with dramatic flair. His larger-than-life personality and endless love of spectacle made him a fan favorite.

The Rangus Power Hour was a wildly popular variety show that aired at several different times each day, starring the colorful mascots and eccentric personalities of Rangusland. Filled with exciting sketches, meat puppets, catchy songs, and wonderfully informative nature segments, with fan favorites such as "What Does a Galactic Hook Worm Taste Like?” the show entertained generations of patrons while introducing the latest Rangus snacks, meals, and exciting food innovations.

The program's cheerful lessons about nutrition, progress, and the importance of trying new Rangus products became just as memorable as the characters themselves.

The Rat Hole was a legendary galactic dive bar tucked away in a forgotten corner of the trade lanes. Though officially independent, it was supplied with delicious prepackaged meals by the Rangus Corporation. Famous for its strange colorful drinks, strange intergalactic clientele, and surprisingly good food, it became a favorite haunt of Carl and Dottie, who spent countless evenings there sketching out new recipes, flavors, corporate takeovers and delicious new business ideas on stained napkins.

More than a few of Rangus's greatest successes began as a conversation in a dingy booth at The Rat Hole. Then, under mysterious circumstances, The Rat Hole vanished without a trace. No distress call, no debris, no records; it just disappeared. Carl spent years searching for the missing bar, convinced that somewhere among the stars it still exists, waiting to serve one last round.

Null and Void were early Rangus mascots discovered by Dottie, who never explained where she found them and would immediately change the subject when asked. Carl initially thought they were great and added them to the original cast of Rangusland. They were featured on the early episodes of The Rangus Power Hour, rendered as adorable cartoon beings. They were ‘souper cute’, had silly antics, and became instant favorites. Then they showed up at a corporate event. In real life. Things did not go well.

The audience reaction was officially described as “collective regret,” and possibly one attendee was eaten. After that, Null and Void were purged from all Rangusland affiliated shows and promotions, episode and promotional materials destroyed, erasing them from the Rangus history. They’ve held a grudge against Carl Rangus ever since. For some unknown reason they especially hate Smart Meats, which they refer to as “a mistake that learned to walk.”

Long considered Carl Rangus's preferred destination for fast and abundant meat acquisition, Esfera De Carne owed much of its appeal to its generous supply of easily harvested game and its close proximity to the Omni Meat Portal entrance.

Carl Rangus evacuated the planet in considerable haste during the Omni Meat Incident, reportedly leaving his Mechanized Suit behind. It has not been recovered.

The extreme cold of Sub Zeroni made it the preferred staging ground for Carl Rangus's efforts to develop a stable meat-and-ice hybrid, a product designed to eliminate the freezer burn losses that plagued Rangus Meats' hyperspace distribution network.

The program was never brought to a successful conclusion. Storage facilities, processing equipment, and a revolutionary ice rail network are scattered across the planet.

A chain of interconnected islands surrounding an active volcano, Lava Del Rey has long been Carl Rangus's preferred retreat, prized for its warmth, scenic terrain, and abundant deposits of naturally occurring Meat Cores.

Sustained extraction of those Meat Cores is believed responsible for destabilizing the planet's geology and reactivating its central volcano. Carl Rangus has continued to return for leisure. Geological activity has spiked reliably on each visit.

Health and Meat Shields are located in the bottom left of the HUD, and also along the left side of the reticle.
You are made up of 3 parts: Head (top), Torso (middle), and Legs (bottom).
Pay attention to your Meat Shields, when one runs out you lose that body part until you pick up another!

Meat parts have abilities that appear in your ability bar at the bottom of the screen.
Each one does something different, so try picking up new meats!
Whack em, Freeze em, Shock em, Burn em

Meat Parts and Weapons can have elements attached.
Dealing elemental damage to an enemy accumulates until it applies the associated condition.
